content.text:
This confirms the driver executes SQL against the `user` table where `avatar_url` is stored. I have the full trace.

h07.
serveUserAvatar — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:168 (Echo handler for `GET /file/users/:identifier/avatar`, registered at fileserver.go:124; reads `user.AvatarURL`)
getUserByUsername — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:715 (wraps the store call with `FindUser{Username: &identifier}`)
Store.GetUser — store/user.go:148 (checks user cache, delegates to ListUsers)
Store.ListUsers — store/user.go:~ (calls the DB driver, populates cache)
driver.ListUsers (DB interface) — store/driver.go (dispatched to the configured backend)
(*DB).ListUsers — store/db/sqlite/user.go:88 (builds `WHERE username = ?` and queries the `user` table, selecting `avatar_url` — the stored data; equivalents at store/db/postgres/user.go:87 and store/db/mysql/user.go:84)

Back in the handler, the stored `avatar_url` (a base64 `data:` URI) is decoded via `parseDataURI` (fileserver.go:737) and written to the response with `c.Blob` (fileserver.go:209).
